decision_reason: The closest unseen pair, exercising on a stepper versus cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions, differs only in cadence in A1. Local thigh orientation provides a potentially transferable posture contrast beyond global inclination. Arm-motion prominence can help describe basketball through seen running, jumping and rowing components without introducing a basketball-specific attribute. Lateral trunk orientation also supplies a physically grounded distinction between the two lying classes, whose A1 difference in smoothness is not implied by their class semantics. Elevator transport and stair direction remain difficult to establish reliably from short-window IMU semantics alone; no elevator-specific or elevation-direction attribute is added. The supplied distances guide these choices but do not establish recognition performance.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: leg_segment_inclination
attributes.definition: Typical unsigned inclination of the instrumented leg segments relative to the gravity axis within a window, considered separately from global body inclination.

levels.Low: Instrumented leg segments remain predominantly near the gravity axis.
levels.Medium: Instrumented leg segments are typically oblique to the gravity axis.
levels.High: Instrumented leg segments remain predominantly near horizontal.

attributes.name: arm_motion_prominence
attributes.definition: Magnitude of active arm movement relative to torso movement within a window, rather than motion shared passively with the torso.

levels.Low: Little arm movement beyond motion shared with the torso.
levels.Medium: Moderate arm movement beyond motion shared with the torso.
levels.High: Pronounced arm movement beyond motion shared with the torso.

attributes.name: trunk_lateral_inclination
attributes.definition: Degree to which gravity is aligned with the torso's anatomical left-right axis, distinguishing lateral lying from upright or back-lying configurations without encoding left versus right.

levels.Low: Gravity has little alignment with the torso's anatomical left-right axis.
levels.Medium: Gravity has partial alignment with the torso's anatomical left-right axis.
levels.High: Gravity is predominantly aligned with the torso's anatomical left-right axis.

operations.reason: motion_intensity: G3 supports observable overall acceleration and rotation magnitude. This preserves a broad transfer axis from walking and running to elevator movement and basketball. Exertion is not equivalent to IMU magnitude, and equipment settings or participant effort can blur adjacent levels.
seen_anchors: running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: cadence: G6 supports repetition rate in repeated limb motion. It retains the existing stepper-versus-upright-cycling contrast and transfers from cross-trainer and horizontal-cycling patterns. Actual exercise rates can overlap, and irregular basketball movement need not have a stable repetition unit; cadence alone should not separate these classes.
target_unseen: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

operations.reason: smoothness: G9 supports sustained rapid fluctuations, distinguishing continuous equipment motion from repeated abrupt movement. Cross-trainer and jumping patterns provide seen anchors for stepper and basketball. Sensor attachment and movement execution affect apparent smoothness; lying orientation alone does not justify different smoothness levels.

impulsiveness: G10 supports short abrupt changes associated with foot contacts or landings, providing transfer from walking and jumping to descending stairs and basketball. Peak events are distinct from sustained roughness. Windows without contacts, cushioning and sensor attachment can obscure the expected contrast; elevator start or stop transients are not guaranteed.

posture_inclination: G1 supports gravity-relative mean configuration, retaining the global upright-versus-reclined distinction needed for cycling transfer. Torso and leg orientation provide expected posture evidence, but forward lean and apparatus geometry can blur levels. This does not itself establish sitting, support forces or local limb configuration.
target_unseen: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

operations.reason: posture_variability: G12 supports changes in gravity-relative body configuration. Seen rowing and walking offer changing-posture anchors for basketball and elevator movement, contrasted with still standing. Limb motion alone must not imply global posture change, and brief windows may omit bends or turns.

rotational_motion: G2 supports angular motion of the instrumented body segments. It preserves transfer from cycling, cross-trainer and rowing to unseen equipment exercise, and from running to basketball. Local cyclic rotation and whole-body turning can produce similar prominence; this attribute intentionally does not identify their source.

seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

operations.reason: translational_motion: G13 supports short-window translation proxies, preserving locomotor progression versus stationary equipment exercise as a transfer concept. Limb cycling can mimic translation, and constant elevator velocity is not directly observable from acceleration. Consequently this attribute must not be treated as an elevator detector or a reliable estimate of displacement.
contrast_unseen: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: motion_regularity: G11 and G6 support recurrence and temporal predictability rather than repetition speed. This transfers structured equipment exercise and less constrained walking to unseen exercise, elevator movement and basketball. Short windows can make irregular activity appear regular; static signals can be predictable without having cadence.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: leg_segment_inclination: G1 supports local gravity-relative orientation from the available leg accelerometers, independently of global posture. It can add a seated-leg versus standing-stepping contrast for the closest unseen pair, with sitting, standing and horizontal cycling as seen anchors. Evidence is the typical orientation of the instrumented leg segments, not an inferred knee angle. The inventory does not specify precise leg placement; lower-leg placement, pedal geometry and large stepping excursions may weaken or erase the contrast. Therefore different ordinal assignments must not be forced solely from the equipment names.

operations.reason: arm_motion_prominence: G2, G3 and G14 support arm angular and linear motion considered against torso motion using the available arm and torso IMUs. This adds spatial distribution of movement rather than another whole-body intensity measure, allowing basketball to share arm-active components with running and rowing while equipment cycling provides an arm-quieter anchor. Passive transmission of impacts, holding rails, optional cross-trainer handles and basketball windows without active ball handling create ambiguity. No hand, ball-contact or inter-sensor phase feature is assumed.

operations.reason: trunk_lateral_inclination: G1 supports the direction of gravity in the torso frame. This separates lying on back from lying on right side through orientation rather than an unsupported smoothness difference, and supplies a low-lateral-inclination seen posture anchor for upright unseen activities. It complements global inclination by identifying lateral orientation, not total tilt. Anatomical interpretation requires consistent torso mounting; torso twisting and transient lateral bends can blur levels. No unseen-class separation is claimed solely from this addition.
target_unseen: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

semantic_redundancy_review: The nine retained concepts remain distinct: magnitude, repetition rate, sustained fluctuation, isolated peaks, mean global inclination, global posture change, angular motion, locomotor translation and temporal predictability. Leg-segment inclination adds local configuration without redefining global posture; its stepper-versus-cycling value is conditional on observable placement and geometry. Arm-motion prominence describes the distribution of movement relative to the torso, not overall intensity or rotation. Trunk lateral inclination resolves orientation within the broader inclined-posture category. These additions do not guarantee unique class prototypes. In particular, standing versus standing in an elevator may remain indistinguishable during constant-velocity or stationary intervals, and no claim of reliable stair-direction or equipment identification follows from semantic distinctiveness alone.
